1.pericope_label: Awake, put on thy strength: sold for nought and redeemed without money

schools.summary: Read the repeated call as deliberate art marking continuity, take the sitting for enthronement rather than mourning, deny that any real sale occurred, and weigh whether Assyria here includes Babylon closely enough to date the book.
Turn the summons on the present church, finding carnal security and a contented outward performance of duty, and ask what anyone ever gained by selling himself to sin.

Furnish the passage from eastern custom and from manuscripts: thrones and footstools where chairs are unknown, one empire whose title passed from Assyrians to Babylonians to Persians, and a repeated conjunction that adds nothing.

Turn the earlier prayer back on the petitioners, who asked God to awake and are now told to awake themselves, with a caution against irregular courses contrary to the law of nations concerning captives.

debates.question: How can Jerusalem be told both to arise and to sit down?

positions.view: the sitting is enthronement, not mourning, since ordinary sitting in the East is on the floor and sitting in state means a raised chair with a footstool, chairs being unknown in Persia except at a coronation
she has risen from the dust, so the sitting implies a throne, set against the seat Babylon was pushed down from
the dust is what she leaves, having sat in it as a mourner

debates.question: Who is the Assyrian, and what follows from it?

positions.view: the king of Babylon, one empire's title having passed from Assyrians to Babylonians to Persians
possibly Babylon under the wider name, which would point to a date when Assyrian kings carried Babylon in their titles, though more probably Sennacherib's defeat offered as a pledge
simply the oppressor who took the people for nothing, the selling being a handing over from which the seller gained nothing

outliers.reading: Alone pauses on the verb for the oppressors' cry to note that the word it names is also the name of the Irish funeral song and that the Arabs have a cry much resembling it, and alone remarks that the Masoretes often retained an apparent mistake in the text although they had evidence enough before them to mend it.

themes: Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean.
Shake thyself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
For thus saith the Lord, Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money.
For thus saith the Lord God, My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.
Now therefore, what have I here, saith the Lord, that my people is taken away for nought? they that rule over them make them to howl, saith the Lord; and my name continually every day is blasphemed.
Therefore my people shall know my name: therefore they shall know in that day that I am he that doth speak: behold, it is I.

7.pericope_label: How beautiful upon the mountains: the watchmen, the bared arm, and the departure

schools.summary: Explain the difficulties rather than emend them: an interjectional idiom for the watchmen's cry, a warrior's bared arm from the battlefield, an idealised return that the histories fulfil only prosaically, and temple vessels borne by Levites.
Take the herald for Christ and the apostles rather than any courier, and read the command to depart as a summons out of the church of Rome, once at the Reformation and once more before the end.
Keep the literal sense first, correct the text where the construction will not stand, and note where a later prophet borrowed the image and where a later writer turned it into a taunt.
Identify the messengers as Jews near the fountain of intelligence rather than official couriers, and read the deliverance as both a mercy to be welcomed and a duty to be performed.

debates.question: Whose feet are beautiful upon the mountains?

positions.view: a messenger from Babylon seen by the watchmen, which is the literal sense of the place
Jews themselves, near the fountain of intelligence, rather than the common posts or the couriers of the government
not the herald of Cyrus at all, but John the Baptist, and above him Christ, and after him the apostles
heralds coming to Zion, reversing an earlier chapter in which Zion was herself the herald

debates.question: What is to be done with the voice of thy watchmen?

positions.view: emend it, since neither the versions nor the moderns have made the construction natural: read all thy watchmen, two letters being alike in sound and one manuscript showing an erasure
keep it and explain the idiom, since the noun with a genitive after it forms an interjectional clause and has almost become an interjection: hark, thy watchers
keep it and let the sentinels simply sing out as they see

outliers.reading: Alone passes a literary verdict on a later prophet, holding that he manifestly took this very image, quoting him doing it, and judging that the imitation does not equal the beauty of the original and that the subjects are not comparable, the borrower announcing only an enemy's destruction where this passage has something infinitely more sublime.

themes: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the Lord shall bring again Zion.
Break forth into joy, sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem: for the Lord hath comforted his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem.
The Lord hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.
Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the Lord.
For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the Lord will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward.

13.pericope_label: Behold my servant: the marred visage and the nations sprinkled

schools.summary: Deny any break between this and the following chapter, weigh who is addressed when the pronoun shifts, and canvass the renderings of a verb that will not yield, while noting how badly the marred visage fits the beauty of later Christian art.

Catalogue and dismiss the alternative referents, arguing that the interpreters' disagreement betrays their perplexity, and take the sprinkling for the doctrine dropped like rain rather than for baptism.

Set the passage in a scheme of three deliverances shadowed under one another, put the promise of prospering first to forestall the scandal of the humiliation that follows, and answer the reading that turns the marred face away from Christ.
Take the prophecy as pointing plainly at one person, on the authority of the ancient Jews and of the sermon preached to the Ethiopian treasurer.

positions.view: the Messiah, the alternatives offered by Jewish interpreters being weak and impertinent and their mutual disagreement betraying their perplexity
an ideal reached by the prophet's own reflection on kings who failed and prophets who suffered, embracing the nation, its prophetic kernel, and the individual who identifies himself with both
the one whose exaltation is the theme, the address passing into the second person and back again

debates.question: Who was astonished, and at whom?

positions.view: the address is to the servant himself, the prophecy turning to the second person and sinking back into the objective
read at him rather than at thee, with the Syriac, the Latin and two ancient manuscripts
the astonishment answers the exaltation, the supreme humiliation matched by the supreme rising

debates.question: What does he do to many nations?

positions.view: sprinkle, keeping the received rendering while admitting no satisfaction with it, since the grammar wants a different construction, and rejecting in turn the readings that make it speech, astonishment, or regard
sprinkle, as a priest cleanses a leper, performed by one himself counted a leper, the rival versions being spring up, startle, scatter, fling away and marvel at him
sprinkle with the doctrine, dropped like rain, and not with baptism

outliers.reading: Alone asks how the idea of the suffering Servant could have arisen in the prophet's mind, tracing it to his own experience of kings who never redeemed the people and prophets who were mocked for speaking the word, so that a law was dawning on him, the power of vicarious suffering and the might of martyrdom, which had then to be worked out on a wider scale still.

themes: Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high.
As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men:
So shall he sprinkle many nations; the kings shall shut their mouths at him: for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider.
